sample_type.evidence_source: [/page/15/Text/11] The present findings showed that teacher expectancy effects are the result of both negative effects of underestimation and positive effects of overestimation. This finding indicates that inaccurate teacher judgments are not necessarily undesirable. Quite the contrary, being overestimated seems to promote students' academic and socio-emotional development, and there was no indication that being substantially overestimated has any detrimental effects (as compared to being slightly overestimated).
